title: NorthForge - Key Management & Access Controls Intake
summary: Intro call to understand NorthForge security requirements for hosting LLM inference. Focus on KMS/BYOK, SSO/SAML and provisioning, RBAC mapping, audit log retention and export, and hosted vs dedicated/private deployment tradeoffs.
topics: Audit logs, SIEM integration, retention policy
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 Type II and recent penetration test PDF (Maya) - target 2027-08-21
SE to produce private deployment network diagram and KMS integration notes (Sean) - target 2027-08-21
Set 90 minute pilot scoping session with infra team - proposed 2027-08-26 (Priya)
Provide initial pricing delta hosted vs dedicated vs private (Maya) - 2027-08-23
action_items: Maya Chen (Redwood) - attach SOC2 Type II and ISO-27001 status notes - due 2027-08-21
Sean Dawson (Redwood SE) - deliver private deployment architecture diagram and BYOK/HSM options - due 2027-08-21
Lena Ortiz (NorthForge) - share current Okta SCIM group schema and list of compliance questions - due 2027-08-20
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-19 16:00 UTC | Duration 57m | Recording available
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Sean Dawson (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (NorthForge Head of Security), Tom Becker (CTO), Ravi Patel (Infra)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, i'm maya, account lead for redwood, quick round of intros?
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: lena here, head of security at northforge, we own compliance and infra gating for new vendors.
[00:13] Tom Becker: tom, cto, internal owner of inference services.
[00:16] Ravi Patel: ravi, infra eng, i'll be doing the config for any private or dedicated option.
[00:21] Maya Chen: great. sean, want to do a quick technical hello?
[00:24] Sean Dawson: yeah hi all, sean from redwood, infra and security integrations, i'll take you through the KMS and net details.
[00:29] Maya Chen: idea for today's call is to map your must-haves around keys, sso, logs and retention and then outline options hosted vs dedicated vs private.

[00:43] Tom Becker: short background — we run sensitive financial models, some PII in prompting pipelines, leadership wants clear controls. big question is can we do BYOK with a hardware module? and what's the difference between hosted and dedicated for auditability.

[01:02] Lena Ortiz: also SOC2, and we need proof of ISO-27001 in the procurement packet ideally; at minimum we need SOC2 Type II report and a recent pen test summary.

[01:12] Maya Chen: understood. we can share our SOC2 Type II and the last third-party pentest summary. we are also in progress on ISO-27001 scoping, i'll include notes on timeline.

[01:24] Ravi Patel: on keys — do you support customer managed keys? like we want our KMS in AWS with HSM, rotate keys on our schedule, and prevent redwood from decrypting at rest.

[01:36] Sean Dawson: yes — for private deployments we support BYOK integration with your KMS/HSM (AWS KMS with CloudHSM or GCP CMEK). for dedicated we offer a customer-managed key option where keys live in your cloud KMS and we use an envelope key flow. hosted api has an optional KM-as-a-service mode but requires legal review for certain data classes.

[01:58] Lena Ortiz: envelope flow meaning the data keys are wrapped by our master key in kms? does redwood have access to unwrapped keys for cache or disk?

[02:07] Sean Dawson: good Q. in private/dedicated BYOK, Redwood doesn't persist the unwrapped master key. the runtime requests short-lived data keys that are encrypted by your KMS; the service keeps only encrypted tokens. for in-memory KV cache there's a transient unencrypted cache in process but we can enable in-memory encryption extension; we'll document that.

[02:33] Tom Becker: you said kv cash? did you mean KV cache?
[02:35] Sean Dawson: yes sorry, KV cache — transcription quirk.

[02:40] Lena Ortiz: about SSO — we use Okta SAML with SCIM for provisioning. we need group-to-role mapping so security admins can control who can kick off models and who can access logs. does Redwood do SCIM and fine-grained RBAC?

[02:53] Sean Dawson: we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC maps to three built-in roles (admin, operator, viewer) plus custom roles in private deployments. SCIM group sync maps Okta groups to RBAC groups; we can accept SAML assertions and map attributes.

[03:12] Ravi Patel: curious about audit logs — we need immutable audit trail, 7 years retention for some records, and ability to forward logs to our SIEM (splunk). can we stream audit logs in real-time?

[03:25] Sean Dawson: yes, we have audit logs that capture token-level, user actions, model invocations, config changes. For dedicated/private you can configure syslog/HTTPS forwarding to your SIEM, retention is configurable. hosted tier defaults to 90 days but enterprise add-on can extend to 365. custom retention like 7 years usually drives private deployment or dedicated with long-term retention add-on.

[03:52] Lena Ortiz: how about tamper-evidence? do logs have immutable storage or WORM support?

[03:58] Sean Dawson: in private you can write logs to a customer-controlled bucket with object lock / WORM enabled. for dedicated we can enable append-only logs to a managed service and provide integrity checksums and signed log bundles for audits.

[04:16] Tom Becker: data residency — some models will run on EU data only, can you pin inference to region and ensure logs and keys don't leave region?

[04:26] Sean Dawson: yes, region pinning available in private and dedicated. hosted model routing we can restrict to regions but legal review for keys crossing borders. BYOK with regional KMS ensures keys stay in-region.

[04:40] Lena Ortiz: model outputs: we need to understand how long prompt and output data is retained and whether it's used for training. our policy forbids vendor-side retraining on customer data.

[04:52] Maya Chen: we can confirm: Redwood does not use customer prompt/output data to train models; retention is configurable. hosted default cache may store artifacts for 30 days for debugging, but with enterprise settings we can disable retention or set retention to zero, or route to dedicated/private where you control storage. we'll include the exact retention controls in the doc pack.

[05:14] Ravi Patel: for private/on-prem air-gap: is there a supported package? our security team is very strict.

[05:22] Sean Dawson: we offer an on-prem bundle that can run in an air-gapped environment with a private control plane. that package includes an offline installer, support for local HSMs, and audit log export to local SIEMs. it requires a longer onboarding and additional license but is supported.

[05:40] Lena Ortiz: ok, questions on encryption-in-transit — TLS mutual auth?

[05:45] Sean Dawson: we support mTLS for dedicated and private; hosted supports TLS 1.2+ and mutual TLS for enterprise customers via mutual auth endpoints.

[05:56] Tom Becker: any SOC2 gaps or open mitigations we should know about?

[06:02] Maya Chen: we maintain SOC2 Type II with no major exceptions in last cycle, i'll include the report and a short summary of remediations for minor findings. also include our pen test executive summary.

[06:12] Lena Ortiz: we also run regular audits, so we'll want a contact for compliance questions and a process for ad-hoc evidence requests.

[06:19] Priya Rao: that's me, priya, i'll be the CSM touchpoint for evidence requests and pilot coordination.

[06:25] Ravi Patel: network flows — if we do private in our VPC, how do you handle egress IPs and peering? we need static egress for firewall rules.

[06:35] Sean Dawson: for private we can provision static egress addresses and peered VPC connectivity. dedicated uses a NAT with fixed egress. hosted is dynamic egress unless you use a dedicated front-end. we'll send the network diagram with IP ranges.

[06:50] Tom Becker: pricing — what's the overhead for BYOK and long-term log retention?

[06:56] Maya Chen: BYOK is included for private; for dedicated there is a small per-region key management fee and an add-on for long-term log retention. i'll include pricing deltas in the follow-up.

[07:08] Lena Ortiz: any concerns about model fallback? if a model is down we need guaranteed graceful fallback to a cheaper family that doesn't compromise PII controls.

[07:18] Sean Dawson: we have routing policies and automated fallback to pinned model variants; for strict compliance you can pin to a private model variant only and disable fallback to hosted variants.

[07:30] Tom Becker: ok can you show us a POC path? minimal pilot to run a sandboxed model on synthetic data and test KMS flow.

[07:37] Maya Chen: yes — proposed pilot: 4 weeks, private sandbox in your VPC, integrate Okta SAML, SCIM sync, validate key wrapping and SIEM ingestion. we'll scope with infra in the next session.

[07:50] Lena Ortiz: timeline — we need procurement answers by end of month. can redwood get SOC2 and pen test by monday?

[07:57] Maya Chen: i'll upload the SOC2 and pen test summary by sunday night, aim for detailed architecture and pricing by tuesday.

[08:07] Priya Rao: i'll schedule the pilot scoping session for 2027-08-26 at 16:00 UTC, sending calendar invite.

[08:15] Ravi Patel: one last — do you have standard SOC2 evidence request templates? helps speed audits.

[08:20] Maya Chen: yes we have an evidence pack and a questionnaire template, i'll attach.

[08:25] Tom Becker: thanks, this was helpful.
[08:27] Maya Chen: recap: redwood sends SOC2 + pen test + evidence pack (Maya), se to send private network + KMS diagram (Sean), customer to share okta schema (Lena) and we'll set pilot scoping (Priya).
[08:40] Lena Ortiz: alright thanks everyone.
[08:42] Sean Dawson: thanks, bye.

End of transcript. Some transcription artifacts noted (KV cash etc).
